translations.literal: Lu Bian's Canonical Classics, thirty scrolls; Wang Shao's Reading Notes, thirty-two scrolls; Wang Tong's Central Discourses, five scrolls; Xin Deyuan's Correct Instructions, twenty scrolls; Taizong's Preface to the Record of Intent, one scroll; also Imperial Model, four scrolls — Jia Xing annotated.
translations.idiomatic: Canonical Classics by Lu Bian in thirty scrolls; Reading Notes by Wang Shao in thirty-two scrolls; Central Discourses by Wang Tong in five scrolls; Correct Instructions by Xin Deyuan in twenty scrolls; Preface to the Record of Intent and Imperial Model by Taizong in one and four scrolls, with Jia Xing's commentary.

sentences.zh: 高宗天訓四卷武后紫樞要錄十卷又臣軌二卷百寮新誡五卷青宮紀要三十卷少陽政範三十卷列藩正論三十卷章懷太子春宮要錄十卷又脩身要覽十卷君臣相起發事三卷魏徵諫事五卷又自古諸侯王善惡錄二卷張大玄平臺百一寓言三卷楊相如君臣政理論三卷陸善經注孟子七卷張鎰孟子音義三卷楊倞注荀子二十卷汝士子，大理評事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong's Heavenly Instructions, four scrolls; Empress Wu's Essential Records of the Purple Pivot, ten scrolls; also Ministers' Tracks, two scrolls; New Admonitions for the Hundred Offices, five scrolls; Essentials of the Eastern Palace, thirty scrolls; Political Model of the Young Yang, thirty scrolls; Correct Discourses for Enfeoffed Princes, thirty scrolls; Crown Prince Zhanghuai's Eastern Palace Essentials, ten scrolls; also Essentials for Self-Cultivation, ten scrolls; Three scrolls on ruler and minister mutually initiating affairs; Wei Zheng's Memorials, five scrolls; also Record of Good and Evil Deeds of Lords and Kings Through the Ages, two scrolls; Zhang Dayuan's Hundred Parables of the Level Terrace, three scrolls; Yang Xiangru's Discourse on Ruler-Minister Governance, three scrolls; Lu Shan'jing annotated Mencius, seven scrolls; Zhang Yi's Sounds and Meanings of Mencius, three scrolls; Yang Bian annotated Master Xun, twenty scrolls — Master Ru Shi, reviewer at the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Instructions by Emperor Gaozong in four scrolls; Essential Records of the Purple Pivot, Ministers' Tracks, and New Admonitions for the Hundred Offices by Empress Wu; Essentials of the Eastern Palace, Political Model of the Young Yang, and Correct Discourses for Enfeoffed Princes in thirty scrolls each; Eastern Palace Essentials and Essentials for Self-Cultivation by Crown Prince Zhanghuai in ten scrolls each; Ruler and Minister Mutually Initiating Affairs in three scrolls; Memorials and Record of Good and Evil Deeds of Lords and Kings Through the Ages by Wei Zheng; Hundred Parables of the Level Terrace by Zhang Dayuan; Discourse on Ruler-Minister Governance by Yang Xiangru; Mencius in seven scrolls (Lu Shan'jing); Sounds and Meanings of Mencius by Zhang Yi; Master Xun in twenty scrolls (Yang Bian) — by Master Ru Shi, reviewer at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 王涯注太玄經六卷員俶太玄幽贊十卷開元四年京兆府童子，進書，召試及第，授散官文學，直弘文館。

translations.literal: Wang Ya annotated Supreme Mystery Classic, six scrolls; Yuan Chu Supreme Mystery Subtle Commendation, ten scrolls — in the fourth year of Kaiyuan, a boy scholar of Jingzhao Prefecture presented the book, was summoned for examination and passed, and was appointed literary officer with a sinecure post in the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Mystery Classic in six scrolls (Wang Ya); Supreme Mystery Subtle Commendation by Yuan Chu in ten scrolls — in Kaiyuan 4 a Jingzhao boy scholar presented the work, passed the summoned examination, and received a sinecure literary appointment in the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 柳宗元注楊子法言十三卷李襲譽五經妙言四十卷鄭澣經史要錄二十卷劉貺續說苑十卷杜正倫百行章一卷憲宗前代君臣事跡十四篇武后訓記雜載十卷采青宮紀要、維城典訓、古今內範、內範要略等書為雜載云。

translations.literal: Liu Zongyuan annotated Master Yang's Exemplary Sayings, thirteen scrolls; Li Xiyu's Subtle Words on the Five Classics, forty scrolls; Zheng Han's Essentials of Classics and Histories, twenty scrolls; Liu Zan's Continuation of Garden of Stories, ten scrolls; Du Zhenlun's Chapter on the Hundred Conducts, one scroll; Former Rulers and Ministers Through the Ages, fourteen sections; Empress Wu's Instructional Records, Miscellaneous Collection, ten scrolls — compiled from Essentials of the Eastern Palace, Canonical Instructions of the Fortified City, Inner Models ancient and modern, Essentials of Inner Models, and similar works as a miscellaneous collection.
translations.idiomatic: Exemplary Sayings in thirteen scrolls (Liu Zongyuan); Subtle Words on the Five Classics by Li Xiyu in forty scrolls; Essentials of Classics and Histories by Zheng Han in twenty scrolls; Continuation of Garden of Stories by Liu Zan in ten scrolls; Chapter on the Hundred Conducts by Du Zhenlun in one scroll; Former Rulers and Ministers Through the Ages in fourteen sections; Instructional Records, Miscellaneous Collection by Empress Wu in ten scrolls — drawn from Eastern Palace essentials, fortified-city canonical instructions, and inner-court model texts.

sentences.zh: 維城典訓二十卷褚无量翼善記卷亡。

translations.literal: Canonical Instructions of the Fortified City, twenty scrolls; Chu Wuliang's Records of Aiding Goodness — scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Canonical Instructions of the Fortified City in twenty scrolls; Records of Aiding Goodness by Chu Wuliang — scroll count lost.

sentences.zh: 裴光庭搖山往則一卷又維城前軌一卷丁公著皇太子諸王訓十卷六經法言二十卷韋處厚、路隋撰。

translations.literal: Pei Guangting's Past Standards of the Swaying Mountain, one scroll; also Former Tracks of the Fortified City, one scroll; Ding Gongzhu's Instructions for the Crown Prince and Princes, ten scrolls; Legal Sayings of the Six Classics, twenty scrolls — composed by Wei Chuhou and Lu Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Past Standards of the Swaying Mountain by Pei Guangting in one scroll; Former Tracks of the Fortified City in one scroll; Instructions for the Crown Prince and Princes by Ding Gongzhu in ten scrolls; Legal Sayings of the Six Classics in twenty scrolls, by Wei Chuhou and Lu Sui.

sentences.zh: 崔郾諸經纂要十卷于志寧諫苑二十卷王方慶諫林二十卷楊浚聖典三卷校書郎，開元中上。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan's Essentials of the Various Classics, ten scrolls; Yu Zhining's Admonition Garden, twenty scrolls; Wang Fangqing's Admonition Forest, twenty scrolls; Yang Jun's Sagely Canon, three scrolls — collating secretary; presented in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Essentials of the Various Classics by Cui Yuan in ten scrolls; Admonition Garden by Yu Zhining in twenty scrolls; Admonition Forest by Wang Fangqing in twenty scrolls; Sagely Canon by Yang Jun in three scrolls — collating secretary, presented in the Kaiyuan period.

sentences.zh: 張九齡千秋金鏡錄五卷唐次辨謗略三卷元和辨謗略十卷令狐楚、沈傳師、杜元穎撰。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling's Thousand-Autumn Golden Mirror Record, five scrolls; Tang Ci's Brief on Distinguishing Slander, three scrolls; Yuanhe Brief on Distinguishing Slander, ten scrolls — composed by Linghu Chu, Shen Chuanshi, and Du Yuanying.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Autumn Golden Mirror Record by Zhang Jiuling in five scrolls; Brief on Distinguishing Slander by Tang Ci in three scrolls; Yuanhe Brief on Distinguishing Slander in ten scrolls, by Linghu Chu, Shen Chuanshi, and Du Yuanying.

sentences.zh: 裴潾大和新脩辨謗略三卷李仁實格論三卷趙冬曦王政三卷景龍二年上。

translations.literal: Pei Zun's Daxing Newly Revised Brief on Distinguishing Slander, three scrolls; Li Renshi's Standards of Discourse, three scrolls; Zhao Dongxi's Royal Governance, three scrolls — presented in the second year of Jinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Daxing Newly Revised Brief on Distinguishing Slander by Pei Zun in three scrolls; Standards of Discourse by Li Renshi in three scrolls; Royal Governance by Zhao Dongxi in three scrolls — presented in Jinglong 2.

sentences.zh: 馮中庸政錄十卷開元十九年上，授汜水尉。

translations.literal: Feng Zhongyong's Records of Governance, ten scrolls — presented in the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan; appointed magistrate of Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Records of Governance by Feng Zhongyong in ten scrolls — presented in Kaiyuan 19; appointed magistrate of Sishui.

sentences.zh: 賈子一卷開元中藍田尉。

translations.literal: Master Jia, one scroll — magistrate of Lantian in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Master Jia in one scroll — magistrate of Lantian during Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 失名。

translations.literal: Name lost.
translations.idiomatic: Author unknown.

sentences.zh: 儲光羲正論十五卷兗州人，開元進士第，又詔中書試文章，歷監察御史，安祿山反，陷賊自歸。

translations.literal: Chu Guangyi's Correct Discourses, fifteen scrolls — a man of Yanzhou; passed the jinshi examination in Kaiyuan, was also summoned to the Secretariat for a literary examination, served as investigating censor; when An Lushan rebelled, he was trapped among the rebels and then returned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Correct Discourses by Chu Guangyi in fifteen scrolls — a native of Yanzhou; jinshi in Kaiyuan, examined at the Secretariat, served as investigating censor; after An Lushan's rebellion he escaped the rebels and returned voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 牛希濟理源二卷陸質君臣圖翼二十五卷李吉甫古今說苑十一卷李德裕御臣要略卷亡。

translations.literal: Niu Xiji's Origins of Principle, two scrolls; Lu Zhi's Diagram of Wings for Ruler and Minister, twenty-five scrolls; Li Jifu's Garden of Sayings Ancient and Modern, eleven scrolls; Li Deyu's Essentials for Governing Ministers — scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Origins of Principle by Niu Xiji in two scrolls; Diagram of Wings for Ruler and Minister by Lu Zhi in twenty-five scrolls; Garden of Sayings Ancient and Modern by Li Jifu in eleven scrolls; Essentials for Governing Ministers by Li Deyu — scroll count lost.

sentences.zh: 丘光庭康教論一卷元子十卷又浪說七篇漫說七篇元結。

translations.literal: Qiu Guangting's Discourse on Healthy Teaching, one scroll; Master Yuan, ten scrolls; also Idle Talk, seven sections; Rambling Talk, seven sections — Yuan Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse on Healthy Teaching by Qiu Guangting in one scroll; Master Yuan in ten scrolls; Idle Talk and Rambling Talk in seven sections each, by Yuan Jie.

sentences.zh: 杜信元和子二卷林慎思伸蒙子三卷咸通中人。

translations.literal: Du Xin's Master of the Yuanhe Era, two scrolls; Lin Shensi's Extended Master Meng, three scrolls — a man of the Xiantong era.
translations.idiomatic: Master of the Yuanhe Era by Du Xin in two scrolls; Extended Master Meng by Lin Shensi in three scrolls — from the Xiantong period.

sentences.zh: 冀子五卷冀重，字子泉，定州容城人。

translations.literal: Master Ji, five scrolls — Ji Chong, styled Ziquan, a man of Rongcheng in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Master Ji in five scrolls — by Ji Chong (Ziquan), of Rongcheng, Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣明脩武令。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Xiuzhou in the Guangming era.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Xiuzhou during Guangming.

sentences.zh: 崔慤儒玄論三卷字敬之，後魏白馬侯浩七世孫，中和光祿丞。

translations.literal: Cui Min's Confucian and Mysterious Discourses, three scrolls — styled Jingzhi, seventh-generation descendant of Marquis Hao of Baima of Later Wei, Guanglu Vice Minister in the Zhonghe era.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian and Mysterious Discourses by Cui Min in three scrolls — styled Jingzhi, seventh-generation descendant of the Later Wei Marquis Hao of Baima; Guanglu Vice Minister in the Zhonghe period.

sentences.zh: 右儒家類六十九家，九十二部，七百九十一卷。

translations.literal: Above, Confucian category: sixty-nine authors, ninety-two titles, seven hundred ninety-one scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Above: Confucian category — 69 authors, 92 titles, 791 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 陸善經以下不著錄三十九家，三百七十一卷。

translations.literal: From Lu Shan'jing downward, not registered: thirty-nine authors, three hundred seventy-one scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From Lu Shan'jing onward, unregistered: 39 authors, 371 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 鬻子一卷鬻熊。

translations.literal: Master Yu, one scroll — Yu Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Master Yu in one scroll, by Yu Xiong.

sentences.zh: 老子道德經二卷李耳。

translations.literal: Laozi's Classic of the Way and Virtue, two scrolls — Li Er.
translations.idiomatic: Classic of the Way and Virtue by Laozi in two scrolls, by Li Er.

sentences.zh: 又三卷河上公注老子道德經二卷王弼注新記玄言道德二卷又老子指例略二卷蜀才注老子二卷鍾會注二卷羊祜注二卷又解釋四卷孫登注老子二卷王尚注二卷袁真注二卷張憑注二卷劉仲融注二卷陶弘景注四卷樹鍾山注二卷李允愿注二卷陳嗣古注二卷僧惠琳注二卷惠嚴注二卷鳩摩羅什注二卷義盈注二卷程韶集注二卷任真子集解四卷張道相集注四卷盧景裕、梁曠等注二卷安丘望之老子章句二卷又道德經指趣三卷王肅玄言新記道德二卷梁曠道德經品四卷嚴遵指歸十四卷何晏講疏四卷又道德問二卷梁武帝講疏四卷又講疏六卷顧歡道德經義疏四卷又義疏治綱一卷孟智周義疏五卷戴詵義疏六卷葛洪老子道德經序訣二卷韓莊玄旨八卷劉遺民玄譜一卷節解二卷章門一卷李軌老子音一卷鶡冠子三卷張湛注列子八卷列禦寇。

translations.literal: Also three scrolls; He Shanggong annotated Laozi's Classic of the Way and Virtue, two scrolls; Wang Bi annotated; New Record of Mysterious Words on the Way and Virtue, two scrolls; also Laozi's Guiding Examples, Brief, two scrolls; Shu Cai annotated Laozi, two scrolls; Zhong Hui annotated, two scrolls; Yang Hu annotated, two scrolls; also Explanatory Commentary, four scrolls; Sun Deng annotated Laozi, two scrolls; Wang Shang annotated, two scrolls; Yuan Zhen annotated, two scrolls; Zhang Ping annotated, two scrolls; Liu Zhongrong annotated, two scrolls; Tao Hongjing annotated, four scrolls; Shu Zhongshan annotated, two scrolls; Li Yun annotated, two scrolls; Chen Sigu annotated, two scrolls; Monk Huilin annotated, two scrolls; Huiyan annotated, two scrolls; Kumarajiva annotated, two scrolls; Yi Ying annotated, two scrolls; Cheng Shao collected annotations, two scrolls; Ren Zhenzi collected exegesis, four scrolls; Zhang Xiangxiang collected annotations, four scrolls; Lu Jingyu, Liang Kuang, and others annotated, two scrolls; Anqiu Wangzhi's Chapter-and-Sentence Laozi, two scrolls; also Guiding Intent of the Classic of the Way and Virtue, three scrolls; Wang Su's New Record of Mysterious Words on the Way and Virtue, two scrolls; Liang Kuang's Categories of the Classic of the Way and Virtue, four scrolls; Yan Zun's Guiding Return, fourteen scrolls; He Yan's Expository Commentary, four scrolls; also Questions on the Way and Virtue, two scrolls; Emperor Wu of Liang's Expository Commentary, four scrolls; also Expository Commentary, six scrolls; Gu Huan's Expository Commentary on the Classic of the Way and Virtue, four scrolls; also Expository Commentary on Governing Principles, one scroll; Meng Zhi Zhou's Expository Commentary, five scrolls; Dai Shen's Expository Commentary, six scrolls; Ge Hong's Preface and Formula for Laozi's Classic of the Way and Virtue, two scrolls; Han Zhuang's Mysterious Purpose, eight scrolls; Liu Yimin's Mysterious Genealogy, one scroll; Sectional Exegesis, two scrolls; Chapter Gates, one scroll; Li Gui's Sounds of Laozi, one scroll; Master He Guan, three scrolls; Zhang Zhan annotated Liezi, eight scrolls — Lie Yukou.
translations.idiomatic: Classic of the Way and Virtue by Laozi in two and three scrolls; annotated editions by He Shanggong, Wang Bi, Shu Cai, Zhong Hui, Yang Hu, Sun Deng, Wang Shang, Yuan Zhen, Zhang Ping, Liu Zhongrong, Tao Hongjing, Shu Zhongshan, Li Yun, Chen Sigu, Huilin, Huiyan, Kumarajiva, Yi Ying, Cheng Shao, Ren Zhenzi, Zhang Xiangxiang, Lu Jingyu and Liang Kuang, Anqiu Wangzhi, Wang Su, Liang Kuang, Yan Zun, He Yan, Emperor Wu of Liang, Gu Huan, Meng Zhi Zhou, Dai Shen, Ge Hong, Han Zhuang, Liu Yimin, Li Gui, and others; Master He Guan in three scrolls; Liezi in eight scrolls with Zhang Zhan's commentary, by Lie Yukou.

sentences.zh: 郭象注莊子十卷莊周。

translations.literal: Guo Xiang annotated Zhuangzi, ten scrolls — Zhuang Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi in ten scrolls with Guo Xiang's commentary, by Zhuang Zhou.

sentences.zh: 向秀注二十卷崔譔注十卷司馬彪注二十一卷又注音一卷李頤集解二十卷王玄古集解二十卷李充釋莊子論二卷馮廓老子指歸十三卷又莊子古今正義十卷梁簡文帝講疏三十卷王穆疏十卷又音一卷莊子疏七卷文子十二卷廣成子十二卷商洛公撰，張太衡注。

translations.literal: Xiang Xiu annotated, twenty scrolls; Cui Zuan annotated, ten scrolls; Sima Biao annotated, twenty-one scrolls; also annotated Sounds, one scroll; Li Yi collected exegesis, twenty scrolls; Wang Xuangu collected exegesis, twenty scrolls; Li Chong's Exposition on Zhuangzi, two scrolls; Feng Kuo's Guiding Return to Laozi, thirteen scrolls; also Zhuangzi's Correct Meaning Through Past and Present, ten scrolls; Emperor Jianwen of Liang's Expository Commentary, thirty scrolls; Wang Mu's Commentary, ten scrolls; also Sounds, one scroll; Zhuangzi Commentary, seven scrolls; Master Wen, twelve scrolls; Master Guangcheng, twelve scrolls — composed by the Lord of Shangluo, Zhang Taiheng annotated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi with commentaries by Xiang Xiu, Cui Zuan, Sima Biao (with Sounds), Li Yi, Wang Xuangu, Feng Kuo, Emperor Jianwen of Liang, and Wang Mu; Exposition on Zhuangzi by Li Chong; Master Wen and Master Guangcheng in twelve scrolls each — the latter composed by the Lord of Shangluo, annotated by Zhang Taiheng.

sentences.zh: 唐子十卷唐滂。

translations.literal: Master Tang, ten scrolls — Tang Pang.
translations.idiomatic: Master Tang in ten scrolls, by Tang Pang.

sentences.zh: 蘇子七卷蘇彥。

translations.literal: Master Su, seven scrolls — Su Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Master Su in seven scrolls, by Su Yan.

sentences.zh: 宣子二卷宣聘。

translations.literal: Master Xuan, two scrolls — Xuan Pin.
translations.idiomatic: Master Xuan in two scrolls, by Xuan Pin.

sentences.zh: 陸子十卷陸雲。

translations.literal: Master Lu, ten scrolls — Lu Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Master Lu in ten scrolls, by Lu Yun.

sentences.zh: 抱朴子內篇二十卷葛洪。

translations.literal: Master Who Embraces Simplicity, Inner Chapters, twenty scrolls — Ge Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Chapters of Master Who Embraces Simplicity in twenty scrolls, by Ge Hong.

sentences.zh: 孫子十二卷孫綽。

translations.literal: Master Sun, twelve scrolls — Sun Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: Master Sun in twelve scrolls, by Sun Chuo.

sentences.zh: 苻子三十卷苻朗。

translations.literal: Master Fu, thirty scrolls — Fu Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Master Fu in thirty scrolls, by Fu Lang.

sentences.zh: 賀子十卷賀道養。

translations.literal: Master He, ten scrolls — He Daoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Master He in ten scrolls, by He Daoyang.

sentences.zh: 牟子二卷牟融。

translations.literal: Master Mou, two scrolls — Mou Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Master Mou in two scrolls, by Mou Rong.

sentences.zh: 傅弈注老子二卷楊上善注老子道德經二卷又注莊子十卷老子指略論二卷太子文學。

translations.literal: Fu Yi annotated Laozi, two scrolls; Yang Shangshan annotated Laozi's Classic of the Way and Virtue, two scrolls; also annotated Zhuangzi, ten scrolls; Outline Exposition on Laozi, two scrolls — literary attendant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi in two scrolls (Fu Yi); Classic of the Way and Virtue in two scrolls and Zhuangzi in ten scrolls (Yang Shangshan); Outline Exposition on Laozi in two scrolls — by the crown prince's literary attendant.

sentences.zh: 辟閭仁諝注老子二卷聖曆司禮博士。

translations.literal: Bi Lu Renxu annotated Laozi, two scrolls — erudite of the Ministry of Rites in the Shenglì era.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi in two scrolls with Bi Lu Renxu's commentary — erudite of the Ministry of Rites in the Shenglì period.

sentences.zh: 賈大隱老子述義十卷陸德明莊子文句義二十卷玄宗注道德經二卷又疏八卷天寶中加號玄通道德經，世不稱之。

translations.literal: Jia Dayin's Exposition of the Meaning of Laozi, ten scrolls; Lu Deming's Textual Glosses on Zhuangzi, twenty scrolls; Xuanzong annotated Classic of the Way and Virtue, two scrolls; also Commentary, eight scrolls — in the Tianbao era titled the Mysteriously Penetrating Classic of the Way and Virtue; the world does not use this title.
translations.idiomatic: Exposition of the Meaning of Laozi by Jia Dayin in ten scrolls; Textual Glosses on Zhuangzi by Lu Deming in twenty scrolls; Classic of the Way and Virtue with Xuanzong's annotation and commentary in two and eight scrolls — in Tianbao styled the Mysteriously Penetrating Classic of the Way and Virtue, a title not used in common parlance.

sentences.zh: 盧藏用注老子二卷又注莊子內外篇十二卷邢南和注老子開元二十一年上。

translations.literal: Lu Zangyong annotated Laozi, two scrolls; also annotated Inner and Outer Chapters of Zhuangzi, twelve scrolls; Xing Nanhe annotated Laozi — presented in the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi in two scrolls (Lu Zangyong); Inner and Outer Chapters of Zhuangzi in twelve scrolls (Lu Zangyong); Laozi with Xing Nanhe's commentary — presented in Kaiyuan 21.

sentences.zh: 馮朝隱注老子白履忠注老子李播注老子尹知章注老子傅弈老子音義並卷亡。

translations.literal: Feng Chaoyin annotated Laozi; Bai Lüzhong annotated Laozi; Li Bo annotated Laozi; Yin Zhizhang annotated Laozi; Fu Yi's Sounds and Meanings of Laozi — all scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi commentaries by Feng Chaoyin, Bai Lüzhong, Li Bo, and Yin Zhizhang; Sounds and Meanings of Laozi by Fu Yi — all no longer extant.

sentences.zh: 陸德明老子疏十五卷逄行珪注鬻子一卷鄭縣尉。

translations.literal: Lu Deming's Commentary on Laozi, fifteen scrolls; Pang Xinggui annotated Master Yu, one scroll — magistrate of Zheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary on Laozi by Lu Deming in fifteen scrolls; Master Yu in one scroll with Pang Xinggui's commentary — magistrate of Zheng County.

sentences.zh: 陳庭玉老子疏開元二十年上，授校書郎。

translations.literal: Chen Tingyu's Commentary on Laozi — presented in the twentieth year of Kaiyuan; appointed collating secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary on Laozi by Chen Tingyu — presented in Kaiyuan 20; appointed collating secretary.

sentences.zh: 卷亡。

translations.literal: Scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Scroll count lost; work no longer extant.

sentences.zh: 陸希聲道德經傳四卷吳善經注道德經二卷貞元中人。

translations.literal: Lu Xisheng's Tradition of the Classic of the Way and Virtue, four scrolls; Wu Shan'jing annotated Classic of the Way and Virtue, two scrolls — a man of the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition of the Classic of the Way and Virtue by Lu Xisheng in four scrolls; Classic of the Way and Virtue in two scrolls (Wu Shan'jing) — from the Zhenyuan period.

sentences.zh: 楊上善道德經三略論三卷道士成玄英注老子道德經二卷又開題序訣義疏七卷注莊子三十卷疏十二卷玄英，字子實，陝州人，隱居東海。

translations.literal: Yang Shangshan's Three-Part Discourse on the Classic of the Way and Virtue, three scrolls; Daoist Cheng Xuanying annotated Laozi's Classic of the Way and Virtue, two scrolls; also Opening Topics, Prefatory Formula, and Expository Commentary, seven scrolls; annotated Zhuangzi, thirty scrolls; Commentary, twelve scrolls — Xuanying, styled Zishi, a man of Shanzhou, who lived in seclusion on the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Three-Part Discourse on the Classic of the Way and Virtue by Yang Shangshan in three scrolls; Classic of the Way and Virtue, Opening Topics, and Zhuangzi commentaries by the Daoist Cheng Xuanying in two, seven, thirty, and twelve scrolls — styled Zishi, of Shanzhou, recluse on the eastern sea.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，召至京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan, summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital in Zhenguan 5.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，流郁州。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era, exiled to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled to Yuzhou in the Yonghui period.

sentences.zh: 書成，道王元慶遣文學賈鼎就授大義，嵩高山人李利涉為序，唯老子注、莊子疏著錄。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, Prince Yuanqing of Dao sent the literary officer Jia Ding to receive instruction in its great meaning; the Songshan recluse Li Lishe wrote the preface — only the Laozi commentary and Zhuangzi commentary are registered.
translations.idiomatic: After completion, Prince Yuanqing of Dao sent Jia Ding to receive instruction in its meaning; Li Lishe of Songshan wrote the preface — only the Laozi commentary and Zhuangzi commentary are catalogued.

sentences.zh: 張游朝南華象罔說十卷又沖虛白馬非馬證八卷張志和父。

translations.literal: Zhang Younan's Southern Florescence Image-Without Discourse, ten scrolls; also Proof that the White Horse Is Not a Horse from the Empty and Flowing, eight scrolls — father of Zhang Zhihe.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Florescence Image-Without Discourse by Zhang Younan in ten scrolls; Proof that the White Horse Is Not a Horse from the Empty and Flowing in eight scrolls — by the father of Zhang Zhihe.

sentences.zh: 孫思邈注老子卷亡。

translations.literal: Sun Simiao annotated Laozi — scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi with Sun Simiao's commentary — scroll count lost.

sentences.zh: 又注莊子柳縱注莊子開元二十年上，授章懷太子廟丞。

translations.literal: Also annotated Zhuangzi; Liu Zong annotated Zhuangzi — presented in the twentieth year of Kaiyuan; appointed temple director for Crown Prince Zhanghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Also Zhuangzi (Sun Simiao); Zhuangzi with Liu Zong's commentary — presented in Kaiyuan 20; appointed temple director for Crown Prince Zhanghuai.

sentences.zh: 尹知章注莊子並卷亡。

translations.literal: Yin Zhizhang annotated Zhuangzi — scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi with Yin Zhizhang's commentary — no longer extant.

sentences.zh: 甘暉、魏包注莊子卷亡。

translations.literal: Gan Hui and Wei Bao annotated Zhuangzi — scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi with Gan Hui and Wei Bao's commentary — no longer extant.

sentences.zh: 開元末奉詔注。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, received imperial command to annotate.
translations.idiomatic: Received an imperial commission to annotate at the end of the Kaiyuan period.

sentences.zh: 元載南華通微十卷張志和太易十五卷又玄真子十二卷韋詣作內解。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai's Southern Florescence Penetrating the Subtle, ten scrolls; Zhang Zhihe's Supreme Easy, fifteen scrolls; also Master of the Mysterious Perfected, twelve scrolls — Wei Gai composed the inner exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Florescence Penetrating the Subtle by Yuan Zai in ten scrolls; Supreme Easy and Master of the Mysterious Perfected by Zhang Zhihe in fifteen and twelve scrolls — inner exegesis by Wei Gai.

sentences.zh: 陳庭玉莊子疏卷亡。

translations.literal: Chen Tingyu's Commentary on Zhuangzi — scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary on Zhuangzi by Chen Tingyu — scroll count lost.

sentences.zh: 道士李含光老子莊子周易學記三卷又義略三卷含光，揚州江都人，本姓弘，避孝敬皇帝諱改焉，天寶間人。

translations.literal: Daoist Li Hanguang's Learning Records on Laozi, Zhuangzi, and the Book of Changes, three scrolls; also Essentials of the Meaning, three scrolls — Hanguang, a man of Jiangdu in Yangzhou, originally surnamed Hong; changed his name to avoid the taboo on the Xiao Jingling Emperor; a man of the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Records on Laozi, Zhuangzi, and the Book of Changes and Essentials of the Meaning by the Daoist Li Hanguang in three scrolls each — of Jiangdu, Yangzhou, originally Hong; renamed to avoid imperial taboo; active in the Tianbao period.

sentences.zh: 張隱居莊子指要三十三篇名九垓，號渾淪子，代、德時人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yinju's Essential Points of Zhuangzi, thirty-three sections — personal name Jiutian, style-name Master Hunlun; a man of the Dai and De eras.
translations.idiomatic: Essential Points of Zhuangzi by Zhang Yinju in thirty-three sections — styled Master Hunlun (Jiutian); from the Dai and De periods.

sentences.zh: 帥夜光三玄異義三十卷幽州人。

translations.literal: Shuai Yeguang's Three Mysteries and Different Meanings, thirty scrolls — a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Three Mysteries and Different Meanings by Shuai Yeguang in thirty scrolls — a native of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元二十年上，授校書郎，直國子監。

translations.literal: Presented in the twentieth year of Kaiyuan; appointed collating secretary, directly attached to the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Presented in Kaiyuan 20; appointed collating secretary attached to the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 徐靈府注文子十二卷李暹訓注文子十二卷王士元亢倉子二卷天寶元年，詔號莊子為南華真經，列子為沖虛真經，文子為通玄真經，亢桑子為洞靈真經。

translations.literal: Xu Lingfu annotated Master Wen, twelve scrolls; Li Xian's Exegetical Commentary on Master Wen, twelve scrolls; Wang Shiyuan's Master Kang Sang, two scrolls — in the first year of Tianbao an edict styled Zhuangzi the True Classic of Southern Florescence, Liezi the True Classic of the Empty and Flowing, Master Wen the True Classic of Penetrating Mystery, and Master Kang Sang the True Classic of the Cavernous Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Master Wen in twelve scrolls (Xu Lingfu; Li Xian); Master Kang Sang by Wang Shiyuan in two scrolls — in Tianbao 1 Zhuangzi, Liezi, Master Wen, and Master Kang Sang were canonized as the four True Classics of Southern Florescence, Empty and Flowing, Penetrating Mystery, and Cavernous Spirit.

sentences.zh: 然亢桑子求之不獲，襄陽處士王士元謂：「莊子作『庚桑子』，太史公、列子作『亢倉子』，其實一也。

translations.literal: Yet Master Kang Sang could not be found; the recluse of Xiangyang Wang Shiyuan said: "Zhuangzi wrote 'Master Geng Sang'; Grand Scribe Sima and Liezi wrote 'Master Kang Sang' — in fact they are one person."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Master Kang Sang could not be found; the Xiangyang recluse Wang Shiyuan said: "Zhuangzi's 'Master Geng Sang' and the Grand Scribe's and Liezi's 'Master Kang Sang' are the same figure."

sentences.zh: 」取諸子文義類者補其亡。

translations.literal: "He gathered passages resembling the masters' texts to supply what was lost."
translations.idiomatic: He assembled analogous passages from the masters to fill the lacunae.

sentences.zh: 无能子三卷不著人名氏，光啟中隱民間。

translations.literal: Master Who Cannot Act, three scrolls — author's name not recorded; a recluse among the people in the Guangqi era.
translations.idiomatic: Master Who Cannot Act in three scrolls — author unrecorded; a private recluse in the Guangqi period.

sentences.zh: 凡神仙三十五家，五十部，三百四十一卷。

translations.literal: Of immortal transcendents in all, thirty-five authors, fifty titles, three hundred forty-one scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Immortal transcendents in all: 35 authors, 50 titles, 341 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 失姓名十三家，自道藏音義以下不著錄六十二家，二百六十五卷。

translations.literal: Thirteen authors of lost names; from Sounds and Meanings of the Daoist Canon downward, not registered: sixty-two authors, two hundred sixty-five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen authors of unknown name; from Sounds and Meanings of the Daoist Canon onward, unregistered: 62 authors, 265 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 尹喜高士老君內傳三卷玄景先生老子道德簡要義五卷梁簡文帝老子私記十卷戴詵老子西升經義一卷韋處玄集解老子西升經二卷老子黃庭經一卷老子探真經一卷老君科律一卷老子宣時誡一卷老子入室經一卷老子華蓋觀天訣一卷老子消水經一卷老子神策百二十條經一卷鬼谷先生關令尹喜傳一卷四皓注。

translations.literal: Yin Xi's Inner Tradition of the High Master and Old Master, three scrolls; Master Xuanjing's Brief Meaning of the Old Master's Way and Virtue, five scrolls; Emperor Jianwen of Liang's Private Record on Laozi, ten scrolls; Dai Shen's Meaning of Laozi's Western Ascension Classic, one scroll; Wei Chuxuan collected exegesis on Laozi's Western Ascension Classic, two scrolls; Laozi's Yellow Court Classic, one scroll; Laozi's Classic of Seeking the True, one scroll; Old Master's Ritual Code, one scroll; Laozi's Proclamation of the Season, one scroll; Laozi's Classic of Entering the Chamber, one scroll; Laozi's Heavenly Canopy Observation Formula, one scroll; Laozi's Water-Dispersing Classic, one scroll; Laozi's Divine Stratagems in One Hundred Twenty Articles, one scroll; Master Guigui's Transmission of Magistrate Yin Xi, one scroll — annotated by the Four Hoary Ones.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Tradition of the High Master and Old Master by Yin Xi in three scrolls; Brief Meaning of the Way and Virtue by Master Xuanjing in five scrolls; Private Record on Laozi by Emperor Jianwen of Liang in ten scrolls; Meaning of the Western Ascension Classic by Dai Shen in one scroll; collected exegesis on the Western Ascension Classic by Wei Chuxuan in two scrolls; Yellow Court Classic, Classic of Seeking the True, Ritual Code, Proclamation of the Season, Classic of Entering the Chamber, Heavenly Canopy Observation Formula, Water-Dispersing Classic, and Divine Stratagems by Laozi in one scroll each; Transmission of Magistrate Yin Xi attributed to Master Guigui in one scroll (Four Hoary Ones).

sentences.zh: 清虛真人王君內傳一卷王萇三天法師張君內傳一卷李遵茅君內傳一卷呂先生太極左仙公葛君內傳一卷華嶠紫陽真人周君傳一卷趙昇等仙人馬君陰君內傳一卷鄭雲千清虛真人裴君內傳一卷范邈紫虛元君南岳夫人內傳一卷項宗紫虛元君魏夫人內傳一卷王羲之許先生傳一卷九華真妃內記一卷宋都能嵩高少室寇天師傳三卷王喬傳一卷漢武帝傳二卷劉向列仙傳二卷葛洪神仙傳十卷見素子洞仙傳十卷東方朔神異經二卷張華注。

translations.literal: Inner Tradition of the Pure Vacuity Perfected Lord Wang, one scroll; Wang Chang, celestial master of the Three Heavens; Inner Tradition of Perfected Lord Zhang, one scroll; Li Zun's Inner Tradition of Perfected Lord Mao; Inner Tradition of Lord Ge of the Left Immortal of the Grand Ultimate, one scroll; Inner Tradition of Purple Yang Perfected Lord Zhou of Mount Hua, one scroll; Inner Traditions of Immortals Ma, Lord Yin, and others, one scroll; Zheng Yun's Inner Tradition of Pure Vacuity Lord Pei, one scroll; Fan Miao's Inner Tradition of Purple Vacuity Princess of the Southern Marchmount, one scroll; Xiang Zong's Inner Tradition of Princess Wei of Purple Vacuity, one scroll; Wang Xizhi's Biography of Master Xu, one scroll; Inner Record of the Nine Florescence Princess, one scroll; Song Du's Biography of the Shaman of Mount Song and Lesser Chamber, three scrolls; Biography of Wang Qiao, one scroll; Biography of Emperor Wu of Han, two scrolls; Liu Xiang's Arrayed Transcendent Biographies, two scrolls; Ge Hong's Biographies of Divine Transcendents, ten scrolls; Master Jiansu's Biographies of Cavern Immortals, ten scrolls; Dongfang Shuo's Classic of Divine Wonders, two scrolls — Zhang Hua annotated.
translations.idiomatic: Inner traditions and biographies of Wang, Zhang, Mao, Ge, Zhou, Ma, Yin, Pei, Fan, Wei, Xu, and other perfected lords; Biography of Wang Qiao; Biography of Emperor Wu of Han; Arrayed Transcendent Biographies by Liu Xiang; Biographies of Divine Transcendents by Ge Hong; Biographies of Cavern Immortals by Master Jiansu; Classic of Divine Wonders by Dongfang Shuo in two scrolls (Zhang Hua).

sentences.zh: 又十洲記一卷周季通蘇君記一卷梁曠南華仙人莊子論三十卷南華真人道德論三卷任子道論十卷任嘏。

translations.literal: Also Record of the Ten Isles, one scroll; Zhou Jitong's Record of Lord Su, one scroll; Liang Kuang's Discourse on the Southern Florescence Immortal Zhuangzi, thirty scrolls; Southern Florescence Perfected Lord's Discourse on the Way and Virtue, three scrolls; Master Ren's Discourse on the Way, ten scrolls — Ren Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Also Record of the Ten Isles in one scroll; Record of Lord Su by Zhou Jitong; Discourse on the Southern Florescence Immortal Zhuangzi by Liang Kuang in thirty scrolls; Discourse on the Way and Virtue by the Southern Florescence Perfected Lord in three scrolls; Discourse on the Way by Master Ren in ten scrolls, by Ren Gu.

sentences.zh: 顧道士論三卷顧谷。

translations.literal: Daoist Gu's Discourse, three scrolls — Gu Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse by the Daoist Gu in three scrolls, by Gu Gu.

sentences.zh: 姖威渾輿經一卷杜夷幽求子三十卷張譏玄書通義十卷陶弘景登真隱訣二十五卷又真誥十卷張湛養生要集十卷養性傳二卷張太衡無名子一卷劉道人老子玄譜一卷劉無待同光子八卷侯儼注。

translations.literal: Classic of Jiwei Hunyu, one scroll; Du Yi's Seeking the Hidden, thirty scrolls; Zhang Ji's Comprehensive Meaning of the Mysterious Book, ten scrolls; Tao Hongjing's Hidden Formula for Ascending to Perfection, twenty-five scrolls; also True Instructions, ten scrolls; Zhang Zhan's Essentials for Nourishing Life, Collected, ten scrolls; Tradition of Cultivating Nature, two scrolls; Zhang Taiheng's Master Without Name, one scroll; Daoist Liu's Mysterious Genealogy of Laozi, one scroll; Liu Wudai's Eight Rays of Shared Light, eight scrolls — Hou Yi annotated.
translations.idiomatic: Classic of Jiwei Hunyu in one scroll; Seeking the Hidden by Du Yi in thirty scrolls; Comprehensive Meaning of the Mysterious Book by Zhang Ji in ten scrolls; Hidden Formula for Ascending to Perfection and True Instructions by Tao Hongjing in twenty-five and ten scrolls; Essentials for Nourishing Life and Tradition of Cultivating Nature by Zhang Zhan; Master Without Name by Zhang Taiheng; Mysterious Genealogy of Laozi by Daoist Liu; Eight Rays of Shared Light by Liu Wudai in eight scrolls (Hou Yi).

sentences.zh: 靈人辛玄子自序一卷華陽子自序一卷茅處玄。

translations.literal: Transcendent Person Xin Xuanzi's Self-Preface, one scroll; Master Huayangzi's Self-Preface, one scroll — Mao Chuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Self-Preface by the Transcendent Person Xin Xuanzi in one scroll; Self-Preface by Master Huayangzi in one scroll, by Mao Chuxuan.

sentences.zh: 無上祕要七十二卷道要三十卷馬樞學道傳二十卷郭憲漢武帝別國洞冥記四卷道藏音義目錄一百一十三卷崔湜、薛稷、沈佺期、道士史崇玄等撰。

translations.literal: Supreme Secret Essentials, seventy-two scrolls; Essentials of the Way, thirty scrolls; Ma Shu's Record of Learning the Way, twenty scrolls; Guo Xian's Separate Account of Emperor Wu of Han's Other Realms and the Cavern Dark, four scrolls; Catalog of Sounds and Meanings of the Daoist Canon, one hundred thirteen scrolls — composed by Cui Shen, Xue Ji, Shen Quanqi, the Daoist Shi Chongxuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Secret Essentials in seventy-two scrolls; Essentials of the Way in thirty scrolls; Record of Learning the Way by Ma Shu in twenty scrolls; Separate Account of Emperor Wu of Han's Other Realms and the Cavern Dark by Guo Xian in four scrolls; Catalog of Sounds and Meanings of the Daoist Canon in 113 scrolls, by Cui Shen, Xue Ji, Shen Quanqi, Shi Chongxuan, and others.

sentences.zh: 集注陰符經一卷太公、范蠡、鬼谷子、張良、諸葛亮、李淳風、李筌、李洽、李鑒、李銳、楊晟。

translations.literal: Collected Commentary on the Yin Convergence Classic, one scroll — Taigong, Fan Li, Master Guigui, Zhang Liang, Zhuge Liang, Li Chunfeng, Li Quan, Li Qia, Li Jian, Li Rui, Yang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Commentary on the Yin Convergence Classic in one scroll — attributed to Taigong, Fan Li, Master Guigui, Zhang Liang, Zhuge Liang, Li Chunfeng, Li Quan, Li Qia, Li Jian, Li Rui, and Yang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 李靖陰符機一卷道士李少卿十異九迷論一卷道士劉進喜老子通諸論一卷又顯正論一卷張果陰符經太無傳一卷又陰符經辨命論一卷氣訣一卷神仙得道靈藥經一卷罔象成名圖一卷丹砂訣一卷開元二十二年上。

translations.literal: Li Jing's Mechanism of the Yin Convergence, one scroll; Daoist Li Shaoxing's Discourse on Ten Wonders and Nine Labyrinths, one scroll; Daoist Liu Jinxi's Comprehensive Discourse on Laozi, one scroll; also Manifest Correctness Discourse, one scroll; Zhang Guo's Great Non-Being Transmission of the Yin Convergence Classic, one scroll; also Discourse on Fate in the Yin Convergence Classic, one scroll; Formula for Breath, one scroll; Classic of Spirit Medicines for Transcendents Obtaining the Way, one scroll; Diagram of Forming the Image Without Image, one scroll; Formula for Cinnabar, one scroll — presented in the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mechanism of the Yin Convergence by Li Jing in one scroll; Discourse on Ten Wonders and Nine Labyrinths by the Daoist Li Shaoxing; Comprehensive and Manifest Correctness discourses on Laozi by Liu Jinxi; Great Non-Being Transmission, Discourse on Fate, Formula for Breath, Classic of Spirit Medicines, Diagram of Forming the Image Without Image, and Formula for Cinnabar by Zhang Guo and others in one scroll each — presented in Kaiyuan 22.

sentences.zh: 韋弘陰符經正卷一卷李筌驪山母傳陰符玄義一卷筌，號少室山達觀子，於嵩山虎口巖石壁得黃帝陰符本，題云：「魏道士寇謙之傳諸名山。

translations.literal: Wei Hong's Correct Scroll of the Yin Convergence Classic, one scroll; Li Quan's Transmission of the Lady of Mount Li and Mysterious Meaning of the Yin Convergence, one scroll — Quan, styled Master Dazi of Lesser Chamber Mountain; at Tiger Mouth Cliff on Mount Song he obtained the Yellow Emperor's Yin Convergence original on a stone wall; the inscription reads: "The Wei Daoist Kou Qianzhi transmitted it to the famous mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Correct Scroll of the Yin Convergence Classic by Wei Hong in one scroll; Transmission of the Lady of Mount Li and Mysterious Meaning of the Yin Convergence by Li Quan in one scroll — Quan, styled Master Dazi of Lesser Chamber Mountain, found the Yellow Emperor's Yin Convergence original on a cliff at Tiger Mouth on Mount Song, inscribed: "The Wei Daoist Kou Qianzhi transmitted it to the famous mountains.

sentences.zh: 」筌至驪山，老母傳其說。

translations.literal: " Quan reached Mount Li, and the old mother transmitted his doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: " When Quan reached Mount Li, the old mother transmitted the teaching to him.

sentences.zh: 葉靜能太上北帝靈文三卷李淳風注泰乾祕要三卷楊上器注太上玄元皇帝聖紀十卷崔少元老子心鏡一卷皇天原太上老君現跡記一卷文明元年老子降事。

translations.literal: Ye Jingneng's Supreme Northern Emperor Spirit Writings, three scrolls; Li Chunfeng annotated Supreme Secret Essentials of Tai and Qian, three scrolls; Yang Shangqi annotated Supreme Mysterious Primordial Emperor Sacred Annals, ten scrolls; Cui Shaoyuan's Mirror of Laozi's Heart, one scroll; Record of the Supreme Old Lord's Manifest Traces at Huangtianyuan, one scroll — the descent of Laozi in the first year of Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Northern Emperor Spirit Writings by Ye Jingneng in three scrolls; annotated Supreme Secret Essentials by Li Chunfeng in three scrolls; annotated Supreme Mysterious Primordial Emperor Sacred Annals by Yang Shangqi in ten scrolls; Mirror of Laozi's Heart by Cui Shaoyuan; Record of the Supreme Old Lord's Manifest Traces at Huangtianyuan in one scroll — Laozi's descent in Wenming 1.

sentences.zh: 呂氏老子昌言二卷王方慶神仙後傳十卷玄晉蘇元明太清石壁記三卷乾元中，劍州司馬纂，失名。

translations.literal: Master Lü's Eloquent Words on Laozi, two scrolls; Wang Fangqing's Later Biographies of Divine Transcendents, ten scrolls; Su Yuanming of Xuanjin's Record of the Great Clarity Stone Wall, three scrolls — in the Qianyuan era compiled by the Jianzhou prefectural aide; author unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Eloquent Words on Laozi by Master Lü in two scrolls; Later Biographies of Divine Transcendents by Wang Fangqing in ten scrolls; Record of the Great Clarity Stone Wall by Su Yuanming of Xuanjin in three scrolls — compiled in the Qianyuan era by a Jianzhou prefectural aide, author unknown.

sentences.zh: 議化胡經狀一卷萬歲通天元年，僧惠澄上言乞毀老子化胡經，敕秋官侍郎劉如璿等議狀。

translations.literal: Memorial Discussing the Classic of Laozi Converting the Barbarians, one scroll — in the first year of Wansui Tongtian, the monk Huicheng petitioned to destroy the Classic of Laozi Converting the Barbarians; an edict ordered Autumn Office Vice Minister Liu Ruxuan and others to draft the memorial discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial Discussing the Classic of Laozi Converting the Barbarians in one scroll — in Wansui Tongtian 1 the monk Huicheng petitioned to destroy that classic; Vice Minister of the Autumn Office Liu Ruxuan and others were ordered to draft the discussion.

sentences.zh: 寧州通真觀二十七宿真形圖贊一卷記天寶中，寧州羅川縣金華洞獲玉像，皆列宿之真，唯少氐宿，改縣為寧真事。

translations.literal: Eulogy to the True Forms of the Twenty-Seven Lodges at Tongzhen Abbey in Ning Prefecture, one scroll — records that in the Tianbao era a jade image was obtained in the Jinhua Grotto of Luochuan County, Ning Prefecture, all true forms of the lodges, only the Lodge of Di missing; the county was renamed Ningzhen in consequence.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy to the True Forms of the Twenty-Seven Lodges at Tongzhen Abbey, Ning Prefecture, in one scroll — in the Tianbao era a jade image of the lodge asterisms (all but Di) was found in Jinhua Grotto, Luochuan, Ning Prefecture, and the county was renamed Ningzhen.

sentences.zh: 道士令狐見堯正一真人二十四治圖一卷貞元人。

translations.literal: Daoist Linghu Jianyao's Diagram of the Twenty-Four Administrations of the Perfected Lord of Orthodox Unity, one scroll — a Zhenyuan-era man.
translations.idiomatic: Diagram of the Twenty-Four Administrations of the Perfected Lord of Orthodox Unity by the Daoist Linghu Jianyao in one scroll — Zhenyuan period.

sentences.zh: 孫思邈馬陰二君內傳一卷又太清真人煉雲母訣二卷攝生真錄一卷養生要錄一卷氣訣一卷燒煉祕訣一卷龍虎通元訣一卷龍虎亂日篇一卷幽傳福壽論一卷枕中素書一卷會三教論一卷龍虎篇一卷青羅子周希彭、少室山人孺登同注。

translations.literal: Sun Simiao's Inner Tradition of the Two Lords Ma and Yin, one scroll; also Great Clarity Perfected Lord's Formula for Refining Mica, two scrolls; True Record of Life-Nourishment, one scroll; Essentials for Nourishing Life, one scroll; Formula for Breath, one scroll; Secret Formula for Firing and Refining, one scroll; Formula for Penetrating the Origin of Dragon and Tiger, one scroll; Dragon and Tiger Disorderly Day Chapter, one scroll; Discourse on Fortune and Longevity from the Hidden Transmission, one scroll; Plain Book from the Pillow, one scroll; Discourse Reconciling the Three Teachings, one scroll; Dragon and Tiger Chapter, one scroll — Master Qingluo, with joint annotation by Zhou Xipeng and Master Rudeng of Lesser Chamber Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Tradition of the Two Lords Ma and Yin by Sun Simiao; also formulas and treatises on mica refining, life-nourishment, breath, alchemy, dragon and tiger, fortune and longevity, pillow books, and reconciling the Three Teachings in one or two scrolls each; Dragon and Tiger Chapter in one scroll — annotated jointly by Zhou Xipeng and Master Rudeng of Lesser Chamber Mountain as Master Qingluo.

sentences.zh: 朱少陽道引錄三卷浮山隱士，代、德時人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shaoyang's Record of Guiding and Pulling, three scrolls — a recluse of Mount Fu, a man of the Dai and De eras.
translations.idiomatic: Record of Guiding and Pulling by Zhu Shaoyang in three scrolls — a recluse of Mount Fu from the Dai and De reigns.

sentences.zh: 張志和玄真子二卷戴簡真教元符三卷楊嗣復九徵心戒一卷裴煜延壽赤書一卷紇干臮序通解錄一卷字咸一，大中江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhihe's Master of Hidden Truth, two scrolls; Dai Jian's True Teaching Primordial Talisman, three scrolls; Yang Sifu's Nine Signs Mind Admonition, one scroll; Pei Yu's Red Book of Extending Life, one scroll; Qian Gan Ji's Preface and Comprehensive Exegesis Record, one scroll — styled Xianyi, Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi in the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Hidden Truth by Zhang Zhihe in two scrolls; True Teaching Primordial Talisman by Dai Jian in three scrolls; Nine Signs Mind Admonition by Yang Sifu; Red Book of Extending Life by Pei Yu; Preface and Comprehensive Exegesis Record by Qian Gan Ji in one scroll — styled Xianyi, Jiangxi observation commissioner in Dazhong.

sentences.zh: 守真子秦鑑語一卷道士張仙庭三洞瓊綱三卷段世貴演正一炁化圖三卷女子胡愔黃庭內景圖一卷道士司馬承禎坐忘論一卷又脩生養氣訣一卷洞元靈寶五岳名山朝儀經一卷賈參寥莊子通真論三卷垂拱中，隱武陵。

translations.literal: Master Shouzhen's Discourse by Qin Jian, one scroll; Daoist Zhang Xianting's Jade Net of the Three Caverns, three scrolls; Duan Shigui's Diagram of Orthodox Unity Qi Transformation, three scrolls; Lady Hu Yin's Inner Landscape Diagram of the Yellow Court, one scroll; Daoist Sima Chengzhen's Discourse on Sitting and Forgetting, one scroll; also Formula for Cultivating Life and Nourishing Breath, one scroll; Scripture of Audience Rites at the Five Marchmounts of the Mysterious Origin and Numinous Treasure, one scroll; Jia Canliao's Discourse on the True Through Zhuangzi, three scrolls — in the Chuigong era he hid at Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse by Master Shouzhen Qin Jian; Jade Net of the Three Caverns by Zhang Xianting; Diagram of Orthodox Unity Qi Transformation by Duan Shigui; Inner Landscape Diagram of the Yellow Court by Hu Yin; Sitting and Forgetting and formulas for cultivating life and breath by Sima Chengzhen; audience rites at the five marchmounts; Discourse on the True Through Zhuangzi by Jia Canliao in one to three scrolls each — hid at Wuling in the Chuigong era.

sentences.zh: 白履忠注黃庭內景經卷亡。

translations.literal: Bai Lüzhong's annotated Inner Landscape Classic of the Yellow Court — scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Annotated Inner Landscape Classic of the Yellow Court by Bai Lüzhong — scrolls no longer extant.

sentences.zh: 又三玄精辨論一卷吳筠神仙可學論一卷又玄綱論三卷明真辨偽論一卷輔正除邪論一卷辨方正惑論一卷道釋優劣論一卷心目論一卷復淳化論一卷著生論一卷形神可固論一卷李延章集鄭綽錄中元論一卷大和人。

translations.literal: Also Discourse on Discriminating the Three Mysteries, one scroll; Wu Yun's Discourse on Whether Divine Transcendence Can Be Learned, one scroll; also Discourse on the Mysterious Net, three scrolls; Discourse on Discriminating the True and Exposing the False, one scroll; Discourse on Supporting the Correct and Removing the Heterodox, one scroll; Discourse on Rectifying the Heterodox and Dispelling Delusion, one scroll; Discourse on the Relative Merits of the Way and Buddhism, one scroll; Discourse on Eye and Mind, one scroll; Discourse on Restoring Pure Transformation, one scroll; Discourse on Sustaining Life, one scroll; Discourse on How Form and Spirit Can Be Made Firm, one scroll; Li Yanzhang collected Zheng Chuo's Record of Central Primordial Discourse, one scroll — a man of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: Also treatises by Wu Yun and Li Yanzhang on the three mysteries, learning transcendence, the mysterious net, discriminating true and false, supporting orthodoxy, Dao versus Buddhism, eye and mind, pure transformation, sustaining life, and firming form and spirit in one to three scrolls each; Record of Central Primordial Discourse collected by Li Yanzhang from Zheng Chuo in one scroll — native of Dahe.

sentences.zh: 施肩吾辨疑論一卷睦州人，元和進士第，隱洪州西山。

translations.literal: Shi Jianwu's Discourse on Resolving Doubts, one scroll — a native of Muzhou, passed the jinshi in the Yuanhe era, and hid on West Mountain in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse on Resolving Doubts by Shi Jianwu in one scroll — from Muzhou, jinshi in Yuanhe, recluse on West Mountain, Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道士令狐見堯玉笥山記一卷道士李沖昭南岳小錄一卷沈汾續神仙傳三卷道士胡慧超神仙內傳一卷晉洪州西山十二真君內傳一卷李渤真系傳一卷李遵茅三君內傳一卷道士胡法超許遜脩行傳一卷張說洪崖先生傳一卷張氳先生，唐初人。

translations.literal: Daoist Linghu Jianyao's Record of Mount Yujian, one scroll; Daoist Li Chongzhao's Brief Record of the Southern Marchmount, one scroll; Shen Fen's Continued Biographies of Divine Transcendents, three scrolls; Daoist Hu Huichao's Inner Biography of Divine Transcendents, one scroll; Inner Biography of the Twelve Perfected Lords of West Mountain, Hong Prefecture, Jin, one scroll; Li Bo's Transmission of the True Lineage, one scroll; Li Zun's Inner Biography of the Three Lords Mao, one scroll; Daoist Hu Fachao's Record of Xu Xun's Cultivation, one scroll; Zhang Yue's Biography of Lord Hongya, one scroll — Master Zhang Hun, an early Tang man.
translations.idiomatic: Record of Mount Yujian by Linghu Jianyao; Brief Record of the Southern Marchmount by Li Chongzhao; Continued Biographies of Divine Transcendents by Shen Fen; inner biographies and lineage records by Hu Huichao, Li Bo, Li Zun, Hu Fachao, and Zhang Yue in one to three scrolls each; Biography of Lord Hongya in one scroll — Master Zhang Hun, early Tang.

sentences.zh: 沖虛子胡慧超傳一卷失名。

translations.literal: Biography of Master Chongxu Hu Huichao, one scroll — author unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Master Chongxu Hu Huichao in one scroll — author unknown.

sentences.zh: 慧超，高宗時道士。

translations.literal: Huichao, a Daoist of the Gaozong era.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Huichao, a Daoist of Emperor Gaozong's reign.

sentences.zh: 潘尊師傳一卷師正。

translations.literal: Biography of Master Pan the Honored Teacher, one scroll — Shi Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Master Pan the Honored Teacher in one scroll, by Shi Zheng.

sentences.zh: 蔡尊師傳一卷名南玉，字叔寶，宋祠部尚書廓七世孫，歷金部員外郎，棄官入道。

translations.literal: Biography of Master Cai the Honored Teacher, one scroll — named Nanyu, styled Shubao, seventh-generation descendant of Song Minister of Rites Cai Kuo, served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, then abandoned office to enter the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Master Cai the Honored Teacher in one scroll — Nanyu (Shubao), seventh-generation descendant of Minister of Rites Cai Kuo of Song, former vice director of revenue who left office for the Way.

sentences.zh: 大曆中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Dali era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Dali reign.

sentences.zh: 劉谷神葉法善傳二卷正元師謫仙崔少元傳二卷陰日用傅仙宗行記一卷仙宗，開元資陽道士。

translations.literal: Liu Gushen's Biography of Ye Fashan, two scrolls; Biography of the Banished Immortal Perfected Lord Cui Shaoyuan of Zhenyuan, two scrolls; Yin Riyong's Record of the Acts of Immortal Zong, one scroll — Zong, a Ziyang Daoist of the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Ye Fashan by Liu Gushen in two scrolls; Biography of the Banished Immortal Cui Shaoyuan in two scrolls; Record of the Acts of Immortal Zong by Yin Riyong in one scroll — Zong, a Kaiyuan-era Daoist of Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 謝良嗣吳天師內傳一卷吳筠。

translations.literal: Xie Liangsi's Inner Biography of the Wu Celestial Master, one scroll — Wu Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Biography of the Wu Celestial Master by Xie Liangsi in one scroll — about Wu Yun.

sentences.zh: 溫造瞿童述一卷大曆辰溪童子瞿柏庭升仙，造為朗州刺史，追述其事。

translations.literal: Wen Zao's Account of the Child Qu, one scroll — in the Dali era the Chenxi child Qu Baiting ascended as an immortal; Zao, as prefect of Lang, later recounted the event.
translations.idiomatic: Account of the Child Qu by Wen Zao in one scroll — in Dali the Chenxi child Qu Baiting ascended; Zao, later prefect of Lang, recorded it.

sentences.zh: 李堅東極真人傳一卷果州謝自然。

translations.literal: Li Jian's Biography of the Eastern Pole Perfected Lord, one scroll — Xie Ziran of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of the Eastern Pole Perfected Lord by Li Jian in one scroll — Xie Ziran of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 江積八仙傳一卷大中後事。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji's Biography of the Eight Immortals, one scroll — events after the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of the Eight Immortals by Jiang Ji in one scroll — post-Dazhong events.

sentences.zh: 王仲丘攝生纂錄一卷高福攝生錄三卷郭霽攝生經一卷上官翼養生經一卷康仲熊服內元氣訣一卷氣經新舊服法三卷康真人氣訣一卷太无先生炁訣一卷失名。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongqiu's Compendium Record of Life-Nourishment, one scroll; Gao Fu's Record of Life-Nourishment, three scrolls; Guo Ji's Classic of Life-Nourishment, one scroll; Shangguan Yi's Classic of Nurturing Life, one scroll; Kang Zhongxiong's Formula for Ingesting Inner Primordial Breath, one scroll; New and Old Methods of Taking the Breath Classic, three scrolls; Perfected Lord Kang's Formula for Breath, one scroll; Supreme Non-Being Lord's Formula for Qi, one scroll — author unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Compendium Record of Life-Nourishment by Wang Zhongqiu; Record of Life-Nourishment by Gao Fu in three scrolls; classics and formulas of nourishing life and breath by Guo Ji, Shangguan Yi, Kang Zhongxiong, and the Supreme Non-Being Lord in one to three scrolls each — author unknown.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，遇羅浮王公傳氣術。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he encountered the Lord of Wang on Mount Luofu and received transmission of the art of breath.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era he met the Lord of Wang on Mount Luofu and received the breath arts.

sentences.zh: 菩提達磨胎息訣一卷李林甫唐朝煉大丹感應頌一卷崔元真靈沙受氣用藥訣一卷又雲母論二卷天寶隱岷山。

translations.literal: Bodhidharma's Formula for Embryonic Breathing, one scroll; Li Linpu's Ode on the Response of Refining the Great Elixir in the Tang Dynasty, one scroll; Cui Yuanzhen's Formula for Receiving Spirit Sand and Using Medicines with Breath, one scroll; also Discourse on Mica, two scrolls — hid on Mount Min in the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: Formula for Embryonic Breathing by Bodhidharma; Ode on Refining the Great Elixir in the Tang by Li Linpu; formulas on spirit sand, medicines, and mica by Cui Yuanzhen in one to two scrolls — recluse on Mount Min in Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 劉知古日月元樞一卷海蟾子元英還金篇一卷還陽子太還丹金虎白龍論一卷隱士，失姓名。

translations.literal: Liu Zhigu's Pivot of Sun and Moon Primordiality, one scroll; Master Haichan's Chapter on Returning Gold of Primordial Florescence, one scroll; Master Huanyangzi's Discourse on the Great Return Elixir, Golden Tiger and White Dragon, one scroll — a recluse; name lost.
translations.idiomatic: Pivot of Sun and Moon Primordiality by Liu Zhigu; Returning Gold of Primordial Florescence by Master Haichan; Discourse on the Great Return Elixir, Golden Tiger and White Dragon by Master Huanyangzi in one scroll each — recluse, name unknown.

sentences.zh: 陳少微大洞鍊真寶經脩伏丹砂妙訣一卷嚴靜大丹至論一卷凡釋氏二十五家，四十部，三百九十五卷。

translations.literal: Chen Shaowei's Marvellous Formula for Subduing Cinnabar in Refining the True Treasure Classic of the Great Cavern, one scroll; Yan Jing's Supreme Discourse on the Great Elixir, one scroll — in all, twenty-five authors of the Buddhist tradition, forty titles, three hundred ninety-five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Marvellous Formula for Subduing Cinnabar by Chen Shaowei; Supreme Discourse on the Great Elixir by Yan Jing in one scroll each — Buddhist tradition totals 25 authors, 40 titles, 395 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 失姓名一家，玄琬以下不著錄七十四家，九百四十一卷。

translations.literal: One author of lost name; from Xuanwan downward, not registered: seventy-four authors, nine hundred forty-one scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: One author of unknown name; from Xuanwan onward, unregistered: 74 authors, 941 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 蕭子良淨注子二十卷王融頌。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziliang's Purely Annotated Master, twenty scrolls — Wang Rong eulogized.
translations.idiomatic: Purely Annotated Master by Xiao Ziliang in twenty scrolls — eulogized by Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 僧僧祐法苑集十五卷又弘明集十四卷釋迦譜十卷薩婆多師資傳四卷虞孝敬高僧傳六卷又內典博要三十卷僧賢明真言要集十卷郭瑜脩多羅法門二十卷駱子義經論纂要十卷顧歡夷夏論二卷甄鸞笑道論三卷衞元嵩齊三教論七卷杜乂甄正論三卷李思慎心鏡論十卷裴子野名僧錄十五卷僧寶唱名僧傳二十卷又比丘尼傳四卷僧惠皎高僧傳十四卷僧道宗續高僧傳三十二卷陶弘景草堂法師傳一卷蕭回理草堂法師傳一卷稠禪師傳一卷陽衒之洛陽伽藍記五卷費長房曆代三寶記三卷長房，成都人，隋翻經學士。

translations.literal: Monk Shi Sengyou's Garden of the Law, fifteen scrolls; also Broadly Illuminating Collection, fourteen scrolls; Genealogy of Śākyamuni, ten scrolls; Transmission of Masters of the Sarvāstivāda, four scrolls; Yu Jingxiao's Biographies of Eminent Monks, six scrolls; also Essentials of the Inner Canon, thirty scrolls; Monk Xianming's Essentials of True Words, ten scrolls; Guo Yu's Dharma Gate of Cultivating the Many, twenty scrolls; Luo Ziyi's Compendium of Sūtra and Treatise Meanings, ten scrolls; Gu Huan's Discourse on Barbarian and Chinese, two scrolls; Zhen Luan's Discourse on Laughing at the Way, three scrolls; Wei Yuansong's Qi Discourse on the Three Teachings, seven scrolls; Du Yi's Discourse on Discriminating the Correct, three scrolls; Li Sishèn's Discourse on the Mirror of the Mind, ten scrolls; Pei Ziye's Record of Famous Monks, fifteen scrolls; Monk Baochang's Biographies of Famous Monks, twenty scrolls; also Biographies of Bhikṣuṇīs, four scrolls; Monk Huijiao's Biographies of Eminent Monks, fourteen scrolls; Monk Daozong's Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks, thirty-two scrolls; Tao Hongjing's Biography of the Thatched Hall Dharma Master, one scroll; Xiao Huili's Biography of the Thatched Hall Dharma Master, one scroll; Biography of Chan Master Chou, one scroll; Yang Xuanzhi's Record of Buddhist Monasteries in Luoyang, five scrolls; Fei Changfang's Record of the Three Treasures through the Ages, three scrolls — Changfang, a native of Chengdu, Sui translator of scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Garden of the Law, Broadly Illuminating Collection, Genealogy of Śākyamuni, Sarvāstivāda masters, eminent-monk biographies, inner-canon essentials, sūtra compendia, three-teachings and mind-mirror discourses, monastery records, and related works by Sengyou, Yu Jingxiao, Guo Yu, Gu Huan, Zhen Luan, Wei Yuansong, Du Yi, Li Sishèn, Pei Ziye, Baochang, Huijiao, Daozong, Tao Hongjing, Xiao Huili, Yang Xuanzhi, and Fei Changfang in one to thirty-two scrolls each — Changfang of Chengdu, Sui scripture translator.

sentences.zh: 僧彥琮崇正論六卷又集沙門不拜俗議六卷福田論一卷道宣統略淨住子二卷又通惑決疑錄二卷廣弘明集三十卷集古今佛道論衡四卷續高僧傳二十卷起梁初，盡貞觀十九年。

translations.literal: Monk Yan Cong's Discourse on Honoring the Correct, six scrolls; also Collected Discussions on Monks Not Bowing to the Laity, six scrolls; Discourse on Fields of Merit, one scroll; Daoxuan's Summary of the Pure Abiding Son, two scrolls; also Record for Resolving Doubts and Penetrating Delusion, two scrolls; Broadly Illuminating Collection, thirty scrolls; Collected Discourse on the Scales of the Way and Buddhism through the Ages, four scrolls; Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks, twenty scrolls — from the beginning of Liang to the nineteenth year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse on Honoring the Correct, discussions on monks not bowing to laity, fields of merit, pure abiding, resolving doubts, Broadly Illuminating Collection, and scales of Way versus Buddhism by Yan Cong and Daoxuan in one to thirty scrolls; Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks in twenty scrolls — Liang through Zhenguan 19.

sentences.zh: 後集續高僧傳十卷東夏三寶感通錄三卷大唐貞觀內典錄十卷義淨大唐西域求法高僧傳二卷法琳辯正論八卷陳子良注。

translations.literal: Later Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks, ten scrolls; Record of Miraculous Responses of the Three Treasures in the Eastern Xia, three scrolls; Inner Canon Record of the Great Tang in Zhenguan, ten scrolls; Yijing's Record of Eminent Monks Seeking the Law in the Western Regions of the Great Tang, two scrolls; Fayin's Discourse on Discriminating the Correct, eight scrolls — Chen Ziliang annotated.
translations.idiomatic: Later Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks; Miraculous Responses of the Three Treasures; Inner Canon Record of Zhenguan; Record of Eminent Monks Seeking the Law in the Western Regions by Yijing; annotated Discourse on Discriminating the Correct by Fayin in two to ten scrolls — Chen Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 又破邪論二卷琳，姓陳氏。

translations.literal: Also Discourse on Smashing Heterodoxy, two scrolls — Lin, surname Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Also Discourse on Smashing Heterodoxy in two scrolls — Fayin (surname Chen).

sentences.zh: 太史令傅弈請廢佛法，琳諍之，放死蜀中。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Fu Yi's memorial requesting abolition of the Buddhist Law; Lin argued against it and was spared death, exiled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Astrologer Fu Yi petitioned to abolish Buddhism, Lin argued against him and was spared execution but exiled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 復禮十門辨惑論二卷永隆二年，答太子文學權無二釋典稽疑。

translations.literal: Discourse on Resolving Doubts in the Ten Gates, two scrolls — in the second year of Yonglong, answering Palace Literary Scholar Quan Wuer's doubts on the Buddhist canon.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse on Resolving Doubts in the Ten Gates in two scrolls — Yonglong 2, answering Quan Wuer's queries on the canon.

sentences.zh: 楊上善六趣論六卷又三教銓衡十卷僧玄琬佛教後代國王賞罰三寶法一卷又安養蒼生論一卷三德論一卷姓楊氏，新豐人。

translations.literal: Yang Shangshan's Discourse on the Six Destinies, six scrolls; also Scales of the Three Teachings, ten scrolls; Monk Xuanwan's Law on Rewarding and Punishing the Three Treasures of Later Dynasties' Kings, one scroll; also Discourse on Nourishing the Living, one scroll; Discourse on the Three Virtues, one scroll — surname Yang, a native of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse on the Six Destinies and Scales of the Three Teachings by Yang Shangshan in six and ten scrolls; laws and discourses on the three treasures, nourishing the living, and three virtues by Xuanwan in one scroll each — Yang clan of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年上。

translations.literal: Presented in the tenth year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Presented in Zhenguan 10.

sentences.zh: 入道方便門二卷眾經目錄五卷鏡諭論一卷無礙緣起一卷十種讀經儀一卷無盡藏儀一卷發戒緣起二卷法界僧圖一卷十不論一卷懺悔罪法一卷禮佛儀式二卷李師政內德論一卷上黨人，貞觀門下典儀。

translations.literal: Convenient Gate for Entering the Way, two scrolls; Catalog of Scriptures, five scrolls; Discourse as a Mirror, one scroll; Origins of Unobstructed Conditions, one scroll; Ten Methods of Reading Scriptures, one scroll; Rites of the Inexhaustible Storehouse, one scroll; Origins of Issuing Precepts, two scrolls; Diagram of the Dharma-Realm Sangha, one scroll; Ten Non-Debates, one scroll; Law of Repenting Sins, one scroll; Rites for Reverencing the Buddha, two scrolls; Li Shizheng's Discourse on Inner Virtue, one scroll — a native of Shangdang, palace ceremonial officer in Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Convenient Gate for Entering the Way, scripture catalog, mirror discourse, origins, reading and storehouse rites, precepts, sangha diagram, repentance, and reverencing the Buddha by various authors; Discourse on Inner Virtue by Li Shizheng in one scroll — Shangdang native, Zhenguan palace ceremonial officer.

sentences.zh: 僧法雲辨量三教論三卷又十王正業論十卷絳州人。

translations.literal: Monk Fayun's Discourse on Weighing the Three Teachings, three scrolls; also Discourse on the Ten Kings' Orthodox Karma, ten scrolls — a native of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Discourse on Weighing the Three Teachings by Fayun in three scrolls; Discourse on the Ten Kings' Orthodox Karma in ten scrolls — from Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道宣又撰注戒本二卷疏記四卷注羯磨二卷疏記四卷行事刪補律儀三卷或六卷。

translations.literal: Daoxuan also composed Annotated Text of the Precept Root, two scrolls; Exegesis and Record, four scrolls; Annotated Karmavācanā, two scrolls; Exegesis and Record, four scrolls; Rites of Conduct Abridged and Supplemented to the Vinaya, three scrolls, or six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan also wrote annotated precept root and karmavācanā texts with exegeses in two to four scrolls each; Rites of Conduct Abridged and Supplemented to the Vinaya in three or six scrolls.

sentences.zh: 釋門正行懺悔儀三卷釋門亡物輕重儀二卷釋門章服儀二卷釋門歸敬儀二卷釋門護法儀二卷釋氏譜略二卷聖迹見在圖贊二卷佛化東漸圖贊二卷釋迦方志二卷僧彥琮大唐京寺錄傳十卷又沙門不敬錄六卷龍朔人，幷隋有二彥琮。

translations.literal: Repentance Rites of the Buddhist School's Orthodox Conduct, three scrolls; Rites for the Weight of Lost Objects in the Buddhist School, two scrolls; Rites of Vestments in the Buddhist School, two scrolls; Rites of Reverence in the Buddhist School, two scrolls; Rites of Protecting the Law in the Buddhist School, two scrolls; Brief Genealogy of the Śākya Clan, two scrolls; Eulogy to Holy Traces Still Present, two scrolls; Eulogy to the Buddha's Transformation Spreading East, two scrolls; Gazetteer of Śākyamuni's Homeland, two scrolls; Monk Yan Cong's Record and Transmission of Capital Monasteries of the Great Tang, ten scrolls; also Record of Monks Not Bowing, six scrolls — a Longshuo man; there were also two Yan Cong in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Repentance, lost-property, vestment, reverence, and protection rites; Śākya genealogy; eulogies and gazetteer; Record of Capital Monasteries and Record of Monks Not Bowing by Yan Cong in two to ten scrolls — Longshuo native (two Yan Cong existed in Sui).

sentences.zh: 玄應大唐眾經音義二十五卷玄惲敬福論十卷又略論二卷大小乘觀門十卷法苑珠林集一百卷四分律僧尼討要略五卷金剛般若經集注三卷百願文一卷玄惲，本名道世。

translations.literal: Xuanying's Sounds and Meanings of Scriptures of the Great Tang, twenty-five scrolls; Xuanyun's Discourse on Respectful Blessings, ten scrolls; also Brief Discourse, two scrolls; Gates for Contemplating Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna, ten scrolls; Garden of Pearls from the Dharma Park, one hundred scrolls; Essentials for Bhikṣus and Bhikṣuṇīs on the Four-Part Vinaya, five scrolls; Collected Annotation on the Diamond Prajñā Classic, three scrolls; Hundred Vows, one scroll — Xuanyun, original name Daoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sounds and Meanings of Scriptures by Xuanying in twenty-five scrolls; Discourse on Respectful Blessings, Brief Discourse, contemplation gates, Garden of Pearls, vinaya essentials, and Diamond Prajñā annotation by Xuanyun (Daoshi) in one to one hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 玄範注金剛般若經一卷又注二帝三藏聖教序一卷太宗、高宗。

translations.literal: Xuanfan's annotation on the Diamond Prajñā Classic, one scroll; also annotation on the Preface to the Sacred Teachings of the Two Emperors' Three Treasuries, one scroll — Taizong and Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Annotation on the Diamond Prajñā Classic by Xuanfan in one scroll; annotation on the Two Emperors' Preface to the Three Treasuries in one scroll — Taizong and Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 慧覺華嚴十地維摩纘義章十三卷姓范氏，武德人。

translations.literal: Huijue's Exegesis on the Avataṃsaka Ten Grounds and Vimalakīrti, thirteen scrolls — surname Fan, a Wude man.
translations.idiomatic: Exegesis on the Avataṃsaka Ten Grounds and Vimalakīrti by Huijue in thirteen scrolls — Fan clan of Wude.

sentences.zh: 行友己知沙門傳一卷序僧海順事。

translations.literal: Xingyou's Biography of the Śramaṇa Known to Himself, one scroll — preface on the monk Haishun.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of the Śramaṇa Known to Himself by Xingyou in one scroll — preface on Haishun.

sentences.zh: 道岳三藏本疏二十二卷姓孟氏，河陽人，貞觀中。

translations.literal: Daoyue's Root Exegesis of the Three Treasuries, twenty-two scrolls — surname Meng, a native of Heyang, Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Root Exegesis of the Three Treasuries by Daoyue in twenty-two scrolls — Meng clan of Heyang, Zhenguan period.

sentences.zh: 道基雜心玄章幷鈔八卷又大乘章鈔八卷姓呂氏，東平人，貞觀時。

translations.literal: Daoji's Miscellaneous Heart Mysterious Chapters with Commentary, eight scrolls; also Great Vehicle Chapter Commentary, eight scrolls — surname Lü, a native of Dongping, Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous Heart Mysterious Chapters with Commentary and Great Vehicle Chapter Commentary by Daoji in eight scrolls each — Lü clan of Dongping, Zhenguan period.

sentences.zh: 智正華嚴疏十卷姓白氏，安喜人，貞觀中。

translations.literal: Zhizheng's Avataṃsaka Exegesis, ten scrolls — surname Bai, a native of Anxi, Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Avataṃsaka Exegesis by Zhizheng in ten scrolls — Bai clan of Anxi, Zhenguan period.

sentences.zh: 慧淨雜心玄文三十卷姓房，隋國子博士徽遠從子。

translations.literal: Huijing's Miscellaneous Heart Mysterious Text, thirty scrolls — surname Fang, nephew of Sui Director of the Imperial Academy Fang Xianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous Heart Mysterious Text by Huijing in thirty scrolls — Fang clan, nephew of Fang Xianyuan.

sentences.zh: 又俱舍論文疏三十卷大莊嚴論文疏三十卷法華經纘述十卷那提大乘集議論四十卷釋疑論一卷注金剛般若經一卷諸經講序一卷玄會義源文本四卷又時文釋鈔四卷涅槃義章句四卷字懷默，姓席氏，安定人，貞觀中。

translations.literal: Also Exegesis on the Treatise on the Storehouse, thirty scrolls; Exegesis on the Great Ornament Treatise, thirty scrolls; Continued Account of the Lotus Sūtra, ten scrolls; Mahāyāna Collected Discourse, forty scrolls; Discourse Resolving Doubts, one scroll; Annotation on the Diamond Prajñā Classic, one scroll; Prefaces to Lectures on Various Scriptures, one scroll; Text of the Sources of Meaning, four scrolls; also Exegesis on Contemporary Texts, four scrolls; Nirvāṇa Meaning in Chapters and Phrases, four scrolls — styled Huaimo, surname Xi, a native of Anding, Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: Storehouse, Great Ornament, Lotus, Mahāyāna, doubt-resolving, Diamond Prajñā, lecture prefaces, sources of meaning, contemporary exegesis, and Nirvāṇa texts by Huijing (Huaimo, Xi clan of Anding) in one to forty scrolls — Zhenguan period.

sentences.zh: 慧休雜心玄章鈔疏卷亡。

translations.literal: Huixiu's Miscellaneous Heart Mysterious Chapter Commentary and Exegesis — scrolls lost.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous Heart Mysterious Chapter Commentary and Exegesis by Huixiu — scrolls no longer extant.

sentences.zh: 姓樂氏，瀛州人。

translations.literal: Surname Yue, a native of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yue clan of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 靈潤涅槃義疏十三卷又玄章三卷遍攝大乘論義鈔十三卷玄章三卷姓梁氏，虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Lingrun's Nirvāṇa Meaning Exegesis, thirteen scrolls; also Mysterious Chapters, three scrolls; Comprehensive Exegesis on the Meaning of the Mahāyāna-saṃgraha, thirteen scrolls; Mysterious Chapters, three scrolls — surname Liang, a native of Yuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Nirvāṇa Meaning Exegesis, Mysterious Chapters, and Mahāyāna-saṃgraha exegesis by Lingrun in three to thirteen scrolls — Liang clan of Yuxiang.

sentences.zh: 辯相攝論疏五卷辯相，居淨影寺。

translations.literal: Bianxiang's Exegesis on the Saṃgraha, five scrolls — Bianxiang resided at Jingying Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Exegesis on the Saṃgraha by Bianxiang in five scrolls — of Jingying Temple.

sentences.zh: 玄奘大唐西域記十二卷姓陳氏，緱氏人。

translations.literal: Xuanzang's Record of the Western Regions of the Great Tang, twelve scrolls — surname Chen, a native of Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Record of the Western Regions of the Great Tang by Xuanzang in twelve scrolls — Chen clan of Gou.

sentences.zh: 辯機西域記十二卷清徹金陵塔寺記三十六卷師哲前代國王脩行記五卷盡中宗時。

translations.literal: Bianji's Record of the Western Regions, twelve scrolls; Qingche's Record of the Pagoda Temple of Jinling, thirty-six scrolls; Shizhe's Record of Kings' Cultivation through Former Ages, five scrolls — through the Zhongzong era.
translations.idiomatic: Record of the Western Regions by Bianji in twelve scrolls; Record of the Pagoda Temple of Jinling by Qingche in thirty-six scrolls; Record of Kings' Cultivation through Former Ages by Shizhe in five scrolls — through Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 大唐內典錄十卷西明寺僧撰。

translations.literal: Inner Canon Record of the Great Tang, ten scrolls — composed by monks of Ximing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Canon Record of the Great Tang in ten scrolls — monks of Ximing Temple.

sentences.zh: 毋煚開元內外經錄十卷道、釋書二千五百餘部，九千五百餘卷。

translations.literal: Wu Jiong's Catalog of Inner and Outer Scriptures of the Kaiyuan Era, ten scrolls — Daoist and Buddhist books: more than two thousand five hundred titles, more than nine thousand five hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Catalog of Inner and Outer Scriptures of the Kaiyuan Era by Wu Jiong in ten scrolls — over 2,500 Daoist and Buddhist titles, 9,500+ scrolls.

sentences.zh: 智矩寶林傳十卷法常攝論義疏八卷又玄章五卷姓張氏，南陽人，貞觀末。

translations.literal: Zhiju's Transmission of the Treasure Grove, ten scrolls; Fachang's Exegesis on the Meaning of the Saṃgraha, eight scrolls; also Mysterious Chapters, five scrolls — surname Zhang, a native of Nanyang, late Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Transmission of the Treasure Grove by Zhiju in ten scrolls; Exegesis on the Saṃgraha and Mysterious Chapters by Fachang in five to eight scrolls — Zhang clan of Nanyang, late Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 慧能金剛般若經口訣正義一卷姓盧氏，曲江人。

translations.literal: Huineng's Oral Exegesis on the Right Meaning of the Diamond Prajñā Classic, one scroll — surname Lu, a native of Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Oral Exegesis on the Diamond Prajñā Classic by Huineng in one scroll — Lu clan of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 僧灌頂私記天台智者詞旨一卷又義記一卷字法雲，姓吳氏，章安人。

translations.literal: Monk Guanding's Private Record of the Words of Tiantai Zhizhe, one scroll; also Record of Meanings, one scroll — styled Fayun, surname Wu, a native of Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Private Record of Zhizhe's Words and Record of Meanings by Guanding (Fayun, Wu clan of Zhang'an) in one scroll each.

sentences.zh: 貞元十三年上。

translations.literal: Presented in the thirteenth year of the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Submitted in Zhenyuan 13.

sentences.zh: 熊執易化統五百卷執易類九經為書，三十年乃成，未及上，卒於西川，武元衡將為寫進，妻薛藏之不許。

translations.literal: Xiong Zhiyi's Transformative Synthesis, five hundred scrolls — Zhiyi classified the Nine Classics into books; after thirty years it was completed, but before presenting it he died in Xichuan; Wu Yuanheng was about to have it copied and submitted, but his wife Xue hid it and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Transformative Synthesis by Xiong Zhiyi in five hundred scrolls — he arranged the Nine Classics into books over thirty years; before he could submit it he died in Xichuan; Wu Yuanheng intended to copy and present it, but his wife Xue concealed the work and refused.

sentences.zh: 李文成博雅志十三卷安國公興貴子。

translations.literal: Li Wencheng's Records of Broad Elegance, thirteen scrolls — son of Duke of Anguo Xinggui.
translations.idiomatic: Records of Broad Elegance by Li Wencheng in thirteen scrolls, son of Duke of Anguo Xinggui.

sentences.zh: 元懷景屬文要義十卷崔玄暐行己要範十卷盧藏用子書要略一卷馬揔意林三卷魏氏手略二十卷魏謩。

translations.literal: Yuan Huaijing's Essentials of Composing Literature, ten scrolls; Cui Xuanwei's Essentials for Conducting Oneself, ten scrolls; Lu Zangyong's Essentials of Masters' Books, one scroll; Ma Zong's Forest of Meanings, three scrolls; Wei Clan's Hand Compendium, twenty scrolls — Wei Mo.

sentences.zh: 辛之諤敍訓二卷開元十七年上，授長社尉。

translations.literal: Xin Zhi'e's Narrative Instructions, two scrolls — presented in the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan; appointed Defender of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Narrative Instructions by Xin Zhi'e in two scrolls, submitted in Kaiyuan 17; he was appointed Defender of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 博聞奇要二十卷開元武功縣人徐闉上，詔試文章，留集賢院校理。

translations.literal: Broad Knowledge and Extraordinary Essentials, twenty scrolls — Xu Yin of Wugong County presented it in Kaiyuan; by imperial decree he was tested in composition and retained as collator at the Academy of Assembled Talents.
translations.idiomatic: Broad Knowledge and Extraordinary Essentials in twenty scrolls, submitted by Xu Yin of Wugong County in Kaiyuan; the court tested his writing and retained him as collator at the Academy of Assembled Talents.

sentences.zh: 開元，召之不赴。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, summoned but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan he was summoned but declined to attend.

translations.idiomatic: Essentials of Ordering the Way by Du You in ten scrolls; Balance in Employing Men by Helan Zhengyuan in ten scrolls, submitted in Zhenyuan 13.

translations.idiomatic: Record of Inspection by Li Zhibao in three scrolls; he was Granary Adjutant of Xinzhou under Emperor Daizong.

translations.idiomatic: Continuation of Quest for the Obscure by Wang Fan; Tang Quest for the Obscure by Bai Tinghan in three scrolls (Guangming period).

translations.idiomatic: Linked Quest for the Obscure by Li Kang; Record of the Three Legs by Lu Jingliang in two scrolls — Eclectic category: 64 authors, 75 titles, 1,103 scrolls.

translations.idiomatic: Six authors of unknown name; from Yu Shinan onward, unregistered: 34 authors, 816 scrolls.

translations.idiomatic: Jiran attributed to Master Fan in fifteen scrolls — questions by Fan Li, answers by Jiran.

translations.idiomatic: Elaboration on Essential Techniques for the Common People by Li Chunfeng — lost.

translations.literal: Presented in the eleventh year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Submitted in Zhenyuan 11.

translations.idiomatic: Six authors of unknown name; from Wang Fangqing onward, unregistered: 11 authors, 66 scrolls.

translations.literal: Liu Yuxi's Transmitted Trust Formulas, two scrolls; Cui Xuanliang's Sea Collected Verified Formulas, ten scrolls; Yang clan's Childbirth Collected Verified Formulas, three scrolls — Yang Guihou; in the Yuanhe era, from Left Reminder demoted to Fengzhou Vice Director and Guo Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Transmitted Trust Formulas by Liu Yuxi; Sea Collected Verified Formulas by Cui Xuanliang; Childbirth Collected Verified Formulas by Yang Guihou (Yuanhe: Left Reminder, then Fengzhou Vice Director and Guo prefect).

sentences.zh: 方九百一十一。

translations.literal: Formulas, nine hundred eleven.
translations.idiomatic: It contains 911 formulas.

sentences.zh: 鄭注藥方一卷韋氏集驗獨行方十二卷韋宙。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu's Pharmaceutical Formulas, one scroll; Wei clan's Collected Verified Solitary Formulas, twelve scrolls — Wei Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pharmaceutical Formulas by Zheng Zhu; Collected Verified Solitary Formulas by Wei Zhou.

sentences.zh: 張文仲隨身備急方三卷蘇越羣方祕要三卷李繼皋南行方三卷白仁敍唐興集驗方五卷包會應驗方一卷許孝宗篋中方三卷梅崇獻方五卷姚和眾童子祕訣三卷又眾童延齡至寶方十卷孫會嬰孺方十卷邵英俊口齒論一卷又排玉集二卷口齒方。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenzhong's Portable Emergency Formulas, three scrolls; Su Yue's Collected Formulas Secret Essentials, three scrolls; Li Jigao's Southern Journey Formulas, three scrolls; Bai Renxu's Tangxing Collected Verified Formulas, five scrolls; Bao Hui's Responsive Verified Formulas, one scroll; Xu Xiaozong's Casket Formulas, three scrolls; Mei Chong's Presented Formulas, five scrolls; Yao Hezhong's Children's Secret Formula, three scrolls; also Children's Longevity Supreme Treasure Formulas, ten scrolls; Sun Hui's Infant and Child Formulas, ten scrolls; Shao Yingjun's Mouth and Teeth Discourse, one scroll; also Jade-Array Collection, two scrolls; Mouth and Teeth Formulas.

sentences.zh: 李昭明嵩臺集三卷陽曅膳夫經手錄四卷嚴龜食法十卷震之後，鎮西軍節度使譔子也。

translations.literal: Li Zhaoming's Song Terrace Collection, three scrolls; Yang Ye's Cooks' Classic Hand Record, four scrolls; Yan Gui's Food Methods, ten scrolls — a descendant of Zhen; son recorded by the Zhenxi Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Song Terrace Collection by Li Zhaoming; Cooks' Classic Hand Record by Yang Ye; Food Methods by Yan Gui (descendant of Yan Zhen, son of the Zhenxi Army commissioner).

sentences.zh: 昭宗時宣慰汴寨。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhaozong's time, comforted the Bian garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he served as comfort commissioner to the Bian garrison.

sentences.zh: 右醫術類六十四家，一百二十部，四千四十六卷。

translations.literal: To the right, the Medical Arts category: sixty-four authors, one hundred twenty titles, four thousand forty-six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Medical Arts category: 64 authors, 120 titles, 4,046 scrolls.
